brief_excerpt: Private credit industry in 2026: market size and growth, key structures (direct lending, CLOs, NAV facilities, preferred equity), recent high-profile failures and stress events, counterparty and liquidity risks, covenant quality deterioration, regulatory scrutiny, and implications for institutional allocators and public market spillovers.

key_findings.statement: FXI is +11.4% vs. January 2022 levels and +93.6% from its October 2022 trough of $19.06
Supreme Court ruled February 20, 2026 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; Section 122 replacement tariff of 15% on all imports effective February 24, 2026 for 150 days (expires July 24, 2026).
BDC total returns Jan 2023 to Dec 2025: ARCC +45.0%, OBDC +47.2%, GBDC +44.0%, FSK +31.6%, PFLT +17.2%; FSK max drawdown from ATH is -34.3% vs -8.7% for ARCC.
IEEPA Liberation Day (April 2, 2025) triggered VIX spike from 20.9 (30-day avg) to 52.3 on April 8 (+150%), the largest volatility spike since COVID-19; HYG drew down -3.7% in the window.
China Vanke entered restricted default in January 2026 when seeking to extend onshore bond payment deadline
IPEV 2025 guidelines, effective Q2 2026, eliminate the PRI safe harbor period and require on-demand revaluation on material events
FSK stock has declined 50.2% from its 52-week high of $20.60 to the current $9.78, vs ARCC up 32.8% since January 2022.
China property high-yield weighting in JPMorgan CEMBI Broad Index fell from 8.94% (2020) to 2.17% (August 2025)
Private credit secondaries averaged 92% of NAV in H1 2025, up from 91% at end-2024
China nationwide residential sales fell to 7.3 trillion yuan in 2025, lowest since 2015; property investment fell 17.2% YoY

open_questions.question: Is Beijing applying selective creditor bailout policy — protecting SOE-adjacent developers (Vanke partial support) while allowing private developers (Evergrande, Country Garden) to restructure? What is the political economy of Chinese developer credit triage in 2026?
open_questions.note: Critical for EM private credit managers assessing residual Chinese real estate exposure marks

open_questions.question: What is the specific regulatory enforcement pathway if GPs are found to have persistently overmarked Chinese developer positions relative to secondary market prices — does Form PF give the SEC actionable standing, or is enforcement limited to investment adviser examination?
open_questions.note: SEC Form PF amendments (effective 2023) increased reporting granularity but do not specify marking methodology. AIFMD in Europe has similar gap. Key question for allocators in Q2 2026 as IPEV 2025 takes effect.

open_questions.question: What specific portfolio event(s) drove FSK's 50% stock drawdown from its $20.60 52W high — was it a dividend cut, Q3/Q4 2024 non-accrual disclosure, or AUM redemption pressure?
open_questions.note: Data shows structural step-down in FSK price, not gradual deterioration — suggests a discrete catalyst. Relevant to whether the discount reflects temporary sentiment or fundamental impairment.

open_questions.question: What is the full multi-year total return gap (price + dividends reinvested) between ARCC and FSK from FSK's 2014 inception, and what share is attributable to fee drag vs credit losses vs portfolio construction?
open_questions.note: Agenda cited a 44pp NAV discount gap — likely refers to total return, not just P/NAV. Requires dividend-adjusted return data from BDC inception.

open_questions.question: Has Citi Wealth or DBRS published a specific timeline for when tariff-driven EBITDA compression will appear in BDC NAV marks — Q3 or Q4 2025?
open_questions.note: Critical for the lag thesis: if the 3-6 month public HY lag is confirmed by analyst consensus, it establishes an early warning window for institutional allocators.

open_questions.question: What is the probability of Congressional extension of Section 122 tariffs beyond July 24, 2026, and what is the administration's stated preference for Section 232/301 replacement?
open_questions.note: 150-day cliff matters for H2 2026 PE/PC deal pipeline forecasting; Section 122 expiry without replacement would sharply reduce trade costs but uncertainty alone is dealflow-suppressing

open_questions.question: What SEC, FCA, or ESMA guidance governs conflict-of-interest in GP-led credit continuation vehicles where the GP both sets NAV and participates as buyer? Any enforcement actions?
open_questions.note: GP-led volume up 202% in 2025 — regulatory lag is a structural risk for allocators

open_questions.question: Are major LP advisory committees (CalPERS, CPPIB, APG) explicitly negotiating ROFR-only transfer clauses (eliminating GP veto) in new 2025-2026 credit fund LPAs?
open_questions.note: This is the single highest-severity structural barrier. If major LPs are making progress here, it accelerates the credit secondaries market timeline to PE-level depth by several years.

open_questions.question: Which specific private credit managers (US BDCs vs European GPs) hold meaningful Chinese property credit exposure, and have any publicly disclosed write-downs or mark-downs?
open_questions.note: GP marks at 3.3x observable market prices suggests either intentional delay or lack of comparable market prices for illiquid instruments. Names needed for allocator guidance.

open_questions.question: What is the current covenant-lite percentage in FSK's and ARCC's direct lending portfolios, and how does EBITDA add-back practice differ between the two managers?
open_questions.note: Fills the covenant quality gap flagged in the research brief — directly relevant to estimating loss-given-default in a tariff stress scenario.
